reserve_note: RESERVE source table. Not announced to the group and not for live use. Caleb asked for Floor 2 canon to be built, held in reserve and kept refined. Do not read it out, publish it, or wire it into a live floor until Caleb releases it.
consumer: none yet (reserve). Future: Encounter Bot / Syndicate when released.

tag_legend.canon: Appears in the books per the ledger (wiki-sourced; nothing here was checked against the novels, see ledger section 0).
tag_legend.inspired: House-game extension or adaptation suggestion. ledger_rows then name the nearest canon basis only.
tag_legend.unverified: Claimed as canon but the ledger row is UNVERIFIED (single fan-site claim) or an open X- conflict says the claim is not confirmed.

confidence_legend: Copied from the ledger Confidence column (VERIFIED / WIKI-ONLY / UNVERIFIED); several rows -> weakest label. null = no ledger row.
out_of_scope: No CR, levels, difficulty, credits or loot amounts: Syndicate rules/10 and the loot decks own those. GM-only spine seeds and house Floor 2 zones are deliberately left out.
how_to_use: Read as a canon reference only while status is reserve. announcement.quote is a ledger-row quote (25 words or fewer) or null; otherwise paraphrase the style.

floor_clock.canon_note: Six days is the Syndicate legal minimum; ten was the normal length guides expected. A one-off cut because fewer Crawlers survived than projected.

house.authority: dcc-campaign/decisions/026-timed-floor-clock-override.md (Caleb, 2026-10-04): Floor 1 = 5, Floor 2 = 10. Read-only citation; this table never edits the campaign folder.
house.why_inspired: The ten-day figure matches the length canon guides expected, so a ten-day house Floor 2 reads as the "normal" version of the floor rather than the shortened one.

fixed_points_keep_absolute.rule: Saferooms close one hour before collapse and eject occupants.
Descending with more than six hours left holds the Crawler in stasis; in the last six hours descent costs no time.

house.beat_scaling_suggestion: Canon patch beats at 31 h and 61 h elapsed (of 144 h) are about 22% and 42% of the clock; on a 240 h house clock that is about 52 h (early Day 3) and 102 h (mid Day 5). Keep the last-6-hours and last-hour rules absolute. All suggestion; no ledger row sets house timings.
house.collapse_order_note: Decision 026 gives Floor 1 collapse order only; no Floor 2 zone-closure order exists. Backlog item.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: Collapse timer is six days, cut to the Syndicate minimum, instead of the ten guides expected.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor1: House Floor 1 = 5 days (decision 026); canon Floor 1 timer not captured here.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: Saferooms close one hour before collapse and eject everyone.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor1: Saferooms stay open until the floor ends.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: Closure by patch at about 4 d 17 h; countdown inside.
First seen with the Krakaren Clone.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: All stairwells exist from the start.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor1: Stairwells appear about 32 hours after opening.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: All 37,500 at minute one; same stasis rule (more than six hours left).

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: Grubs replace rats as janitor mobs, with a pupa-and-Vespa life cycle and a spawn cap.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: 1 to 15 grubs per corpse up to a per-quadrant cap.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: Relieving yourself outside a bathroom now summons a Rage Elemental.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor1: A bug-fix scolding about hallway use; no penalty.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: Human-born Crawlers and all humans; pets exempt; ends at collapse.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: Saferooms gain a mailbox for the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: Subscribers get one tome per floor; others see an error line.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: The audience economy turns on: follows, favorites, ratings, revised patronage.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor1: Viewers could not follow or favorite.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: Switched on at the opening announcement.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: Floor 2 introduces deliberate running storylines (Rev-Up) and media set-pieces, not just stand-alone mobs.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: Rev-Up pyramid scheme, Death Watch, Rage Elemental trap.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: The grid is split into regions that never connect, and halls are narrower.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: Unconnected regional sections; narrower arteries; cinderblock.

floor_differences_from_floor_1.difference: Roughly 1.29 million Crawlers entered Floor 2 after the Floor 1 collapse killed over 700,000.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor1: Not captured as a row; Floor 1 ended in a collapse that killed over 700,000.
floor_differences_from_floor_1.floor2: 1,292,526 at the countdown start; under one million by the third day.

system_announcements.voice: Cascadia presents like a cheerful corporate host: congratulates, pads policy with sales language, then drops an ominous rule in a tidy sentence. Every announcement ends with a bright kill-kill-kill line. Patch notes arrive after a recap episode and read like apologetic changelogs. Not announced to the group in this reserve table.

beats.when: about 7 h after the floor opens, after episode 4
beats.what: Count under projections, timer cut to the minimum, wait until the last moment to descend, follows/favorites on, revised patronage, bathroom penalty, sign-off.

quotes.quote: You have six days to find a staircase down.
Once again, we urge you all to wait until the last possible moment to descend.
This elemental will kill them and everyone in their party before they can get their pants back up.
Have fun out there, and remember to kill, kill, kill!

beats.when: about 4 d 17 h before collapse (after episode 5)
beats.what: Satan's Lil' Hedgehogs relocated; saferooms will close one hour before collapse.

quotes.quote: The Satan's Lil' Hedgehogs mob is relocated to a deeper floor.

beats.when: about 3 d 11 h before collapse (daily announcement)
beats.what: Guides may explain Floor 3 race/class selection; non-sapient mobs no longer disintegrate in stairwells; Vespa cut; grubs have a 50% chance to pupate.

quotes.quote: Game Guides can now begin explaining Third Floor race/class selection.
Non-sapient mobs that enter a stairwell will no longer disintegrate.

beats.what: A recap episode justifies the bathroom trap; the announcement says the rule ends at the floor collapse.
Crawlers can begin descending without losing time.

quotes.quote: Crawlers can begin descending to the Third Floor without losing time.

timeline_by_countdown.event: Floor opens; Crawlers can start exploring.
Countdown timer starts; 1,292,526 Crawlers left; Dungeon Crawler World: Earth episode 4 airs.
Cascadia's introductory announcement; ratings go live.
Patch: Hedgehogs relocated; saferooms will close one hour before collapse.
Daily announcement: guides may explain Floor 3; stairwell no-disintegrate; Vespa and pupa patch; under one million Crawlers.

zones.name: The Second Floor (floor-wide rules)
zones.name_note: Canon name: The Second Floor, the last Tutorial floor. No house name or house zone map exists yet (reserve).
zones.staging: A giant grid of narrower cinderblock halls over cracked white concrete, cut into regions that never connect. All stairwells exist from minute one, so the floor is a race against the clock rather than a search for a key. Bosses may now leave their rooms, saferooms close an hour before the end, and the audience machinery (follows, favorites, ratings) is live.

announcement.style: Cascadia sounds like a cheerful corporate announcer padding bad news with sales language; the one stern note is scolding Crawlers about bathrooms.

hazards.name: Bosses leave their chambers
hazards.what: From this floor a boss can burst out and hit Crawlers in the hall; the first time earns a deadpan achievement. Floor 1 bosses never did this.

hazards.name: Unbreakable-looking walls
hazards.what: Cinderblock cracks but does not fully break, so Crawlers cannot dig out; a boss can still wreck it. The walls are coated in places with an orange-tinted green lichen.
hazards.note: A fan wiki says the lichen gives the dim light (M-899, UNVERIFIED).

features.name: Restroom portals and the one private place
features.what: Mismatched doors about every quarter mile open on the Crawler's own stall; the stall is the only spot shielded from cameras.

features.name: Stairwells (all present at the start)
features.what: Every Borough and City boss chamber holds one. Descending with more than six hours left means stasis until the floor ends; in the last six hours it costs no time.

features.name: Tutorial Guild Halls
features.what: Still open on Floors 1-3; Game Guides are hidden from ordinary viewers; in the last days guides may begin explaining Floor 3 race/class selection.

features.name: Ratings go live
features.what: Follows, favorites and ratings switch on after the opening announcement; numbers fill in slowly.

features.name: Revised patronage
features.what: Three patrons per Crawler, auctions on later floors, and a patron who pays more gets better Benefactor Boxes for the Crawler (no amounts recorded here).
features.note: Start floor of the auctions differs between sources (X-061).

zones.name: Floor 2 saferooms (closure, mailbox, staffed and unstaffed)
zones.staging: Saferooms are lifted whole from Earth (a storm shelter, an industrial kitchen, a chicken restaurant). Some have a Bopca Protector who cooks and fusses; some are bare. The new things on this floor are the mailbox and the closing hour: an hour before collapse the room spits everyone out and a countdown tells you it is coming.

announcement.style: The closure arrives as a cheerful patch note after a recap episode; the System frames it as fixing Crawlers who stayed, partied and died in Floor 1 saferooms.
announcement.quote: Starting on the Second Floor, all safe rooms close one hour before level collapse, teleporting any crawlers still inside to just outside the room.

hazards.name: Saferoom closure (one hour before collapse)
hazards.what: Anyone still inside is teleported just outside; a Time to Safe Room Closure countdown shows inside. Added by patch about 4 d 17 h before collapse, so before then a room could be used to wait out the clock.

features.name: Storm-shelter saferoom with mailbox
features.what: Suburban-style mailbox with the flag up. Only Dungeon Book of the Floor Club (or similar) subscribers can open it; everyone else gets a System error line. One tome per floor.

features.name: Big Shot Chicken (staffed by Qwist)
features.what: A dusty chicken restaurant saferoom run by a Bopca Protector who grooms and feeds guests. Where the Rage Elemental sieges the door.

features.name: Unstaffed saferoom with Mana Toast
features.what: A toaster oven gives each Crawler one piece of mana-restoring toast; no food or staff. The Book 1 recap puts it in the Kobold quadrant, in an industrial kitchen with a working freezer.
features.note: The kitchen link (M-733) is recap-transcript only, WIKI-ONLY.

features.name: Unnamed hallway saferoom (Team Li Na escape)
features.what: The nearest saferoom to the frozen Death Watch ambush; the four survivors slip past the fight into it and patch up the manager with a healing potion.

features.name: Cots or private rooms
features.what: Every saferoom has dusty cots or private rooms, free or rented on this floor.

features.name: Floor Club tome is lost at collapse
features.what: A tome not collected before the floor collapses is destroyed (rule from a later book, applies to every floor).
features.note: Source cite is B6 ch2; kept because it governs the Floor 2 mailbox.

zones.name: Rev-Up distillery and the Krakaren Clone
zones.name_note: Canon: the Rev-Up pyramid-scheme storyline. At least three Krakaren Clone instances exist on the floor.
zones.staging: A moonshine distillery run like a multi-level-marketing scheme: sniffly clurichauns slinging rocks at the bottom, leaf-suited Laminak "managers" above, and a screaming tentacled Krakaren Clone at the top behind a Live-Laugh-Love sign. The boss does not wait in her room: she blasts out through the walls. Contact with the lower tiers gives the Taint (no healing), the boss adds Vigorous Measles, and the cure-by-prevention is a smoothie blended from moonshine and a Laminak corpse on a bicycle blender.

announcement.style: Mob and boss nameplates read like spam pamphlets and anti-vaccine parody; the achievement that fires when the boss bursts out is a cheerful "welcome to the second floor."
announcement.quote: Welcome to the second floor, bitches.

mobs.name: Unvaccinated Clurichaun Rev-Up Consultant
mobs.what: Runny-nosed, troll-like fairy cousin of leprechauns in green overalls: slingshot or grapple, very fast, contact leaves lime-green residue and the Taint for five minutes; corpses ooze toxic liquid.

mobs.name: Laminak / Laminak Rev-Up Consultant Elite
mobs.what: Fat, crow-sized fairies; the Elites look like winged soccer moms in leaf pantsuits, cast Magic Missile, resist health-seeping attacks and believe working for Rev-Up will get them to Floor 3.

mobs.name: Krakaren Clone (Second Floor)
mobs.what: Twenty-foot immobile octopus with screaming human-mouth tentacles, Taint snot and a Vigorous Measles mist. Bursts out of its chamber. At least three exist; its nameplate stresses it is a copy, not the Krakaren itself.
mobs.note: Neighborhood Boss per the wiki, the recap and the AI nameplate text (M-709); one fan table says Borough (X-059).

hazards.name: The Taint
hazards.what: Five-minute debuff: no healing by any method. Spread by touching clurichauns, their corpses or the boss snot.

hazards.name: Vigorous Measles mist
hazards.what: Communicable disease sprayed as an aerosol by the boss; prevented, not cured, by the Immunity Smoothie.

hazards.name: Boss breaks out through the walls
hazards.what: The clone blasts her door open and flails tentacles through cinderblock into the next room.

features.name: Rev-Up moonshine distillery
features.what: Bolted-down moonshine tub, jugs, Alchemy Table and two bicycle-powered blenders with the smoothie recipe; the door to the boss chamber is under cut-out Live, Laugh, Love letters.

features.name: Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie
features.what: Temporary immunity to the Taint and Vigorous Measles; also Buzzed (drunk) debuff. Brewed from moonshine plus a Laminak Elite corpse.

features.name: Location Manager Damien (unseen)
features.what: A hidden Borant manager who oversees the Rev-Up area; dying Laminaks scream for him and he never comes.

zones.name: Brindle Grub fields (janitor cycle: grub, pupa, Vespa)
zones.staging: The more things die in a quadrant, the more cat-sized worms the floor spawns to eat them. Kill too fast and the hall fills with grubs; leave them and they grow into cow-tailed grubs, then pulsating human-sized sacs with a visible countdown, then acid-spitting hornets. The trap for GMs and Crawlers is that destroying corpses does not stop new grubs.

announcement.style: Patch notes announce the grub problem was too lethal and quietly nerf it by half; the tone is a store manager adjusting inventory.
announcement.quote: Brindle Grubs continue to generate on every corpse, but now have only a 50% chance of advancing to the pupa stage.

mobs.name: Brindle Grub
mobs.what: Fuzzy cat-sized worm that eats corpses and grows; squeaks, bursts into goo; drops alchemy hemolymph.

mobs.name: Cow-Tailed Brindle Grub
mobs.what: Final pre-pupa form; bigger, with ineffective whip tails.

mobs.name: Grub pupa
mobs.what: Human-sized wet sac with flashing lights and a countdown of at least ten hours; bursting it early spills convulsing "uncooked" creatures.
mobs.note: Fan table says a damaged sac releases Vespas (X-060).

mobs.name: Brindled Vespa
mobs.what: Hornet-like final stage that spits acid goo; population was halved by a patch.

hazards.name: Grub flood (spawn cap per quadrant)
hazards.what: One to fifteen grubs per corpse, up to a hard cap per quadrant; destroying corpses does not stop it. A big fight can bury a neighborhood and drive a camp out.

hazards.name: Pupa countdown
hazards.what: A visible timer means "move on": when it ends a Vespa hatches. After the patch only half of grubs reach this stage.

hazards.name: Vespa acid spit
hazards.what: Ranged acid globs from airborne hornets.

features.name: Grub patch notes
features.what: About 3 d 11 h before collapse the daily announcement halves the Vespas, lowers their acid, and gives grubs a 50% chance to pupate.

zones.name: Kobold training grounds and the dog pound (Ralph)
zones.name_note: Canon boss: Ralph, a Frenzied Gerbil, a Neighborhood Boss.
zones.staging: Heavy distorted-barking music pours from a converted municipal dog pound: three hallways of cages, injured dingoes inside. Feeding a caged dingo a pet biscuit turns it from hostile to friendly, so the boss fight can be won by cashing in the animals the kobolds abuse. About forty kobolds march in with Ralph in a small cage; when the dingoes are loosed, one swallows him, but he is not dead. The prize room is a pet reward room with a line of caged monsters.

announcement.style: The boss intro is a darkly funny history lesson about gerbils and the Black Death, then a flat "you might want to duck."

mobs.name: Danger Dingo
mobs.what: Mastiff-sized canines with huge fangs and heavy-metal corpse-paint faces, ridden by kobolds; many are caged and hurt in the pound. The recap counts fourteen fed in the cages and thirteen that scatter after Ralph dies, wiping out new grubs.
mobs.note: Fourteen to thirteen fits the first-fed dingo dying when Ralph bursts out of it (M-420); that link is a reading, not a source claim.

mobs.name: Kobold / Kobold Rider
mobs.what: Yappy, fearless chihuahua-like brawlers who charge on dingoes with feathered lances.

mobs.name: Ralph the Frenzied Gerbil
mobs.what: Champion pit fighter of the kobold grounds: an absurdly cute gerbil whose mouth opens impossibly wide. Survives being swallowed and bursts out of the dingo.

mobs.name: Mongoliensis chick (Mongo)
mobs.what: Aggressive pet-class chick in one of the ten cages of the pet reward room; needs repeated feeding and time to bond.
mobs.note: "Last cage" is web-only (M-521); the ten-cage count is now VERIFIED (M-710). A fan wiki adds that he bonded after Donut saved him from a Brindled Vespa (M-915, UNVERIFIED).

mobs.name: Dingo control spell (kobold slavery)
mobs.what: A fan bestiary says kobolds hold the dingoes by a control spell that breaks in the Ralph fight.
mobs.note: UNVERIFIED single fan-site claim. The Fandom Ralph page and the recap both have a kobold simply opening the cages, with no spell named (M-913).

hazards.name: Distorted boss music
hazards.what: The chamber music is so loud the pair switch to chat; plan on no shouted calls.

hazards.name: Cages open mid-fight
hazards.what: A surviving kobold slinks to the wall and releases the dingoes from their cages mid-fight; dingoes fed beforehand turn on the kobolds instead.
hazards.note: Retagged canon in Pass 35: the release at the wall is on the Fandom Ralph page (cite B1 ch45) and in the recap (M-913). A wall button as such is still web-only (M-522).

features.name: Feed the caged dingoes (PETA Enthusiast)
features.what: A pet biscuit turns a hostile dingo to neutral; a neat non-lethal solve that changes the boss fight.

features.name: Pet reward room (Menagerie)
features.what: After Ralph: a reward room where a Kobold-corpse key opens the cages. One key means one pet. The key is attuned to kobolds and breaks after one use by anyone else. An unbonded pet stays behind at collapse and will not stay in a saferoom uncaged.
features.note: Menagerie row A-083 is WIKI-ONLY (incomplete infobox).

features.name: Reward room cage line (ten cages)
features.what: Ten cages of pets: a loud long-beaked Juvenile Riven Wing, a green slime, a rat, a two-legged mohawked Tummy Acher, a Brindle Grub and the mongoliensis chick. Donut passes on the Tummy Acher for Mongo.
features.note: Cage count and pet list now VERIFIED (wiki + recap); supersedes web-only M-M-521.

features.name: Generic reward-room achievement (Ceramic Dalmatian)
features.what: The generic reward-room achievement text; the floor it first fires on is still an open conflict.
features.note: A-056 is UNVERIFIED (F9 page vs F2 master list).

zones.name: Mind Horror quadrants and the rest of the Floor 2 roster
zones.staging: Floating brain-jellyfish drift in slow packs on the way to the saferoom; the danger is a psionic headache rather than a bite. Elsewhere the roster is thin: a hedgehog mob that was pulled, a rumoured acid-dart spitter, and a blimp-shaped neighborhood boss the party killed off-screen.

announcement.style: Mob nameplates stay in the deadpan-snarky voice; the hedgehog removal is a cheerful patch-note apology.
announcement.quote: The Satan's Lil' Hedgehogs mob is relocated to a deeper floor.

mobs.name: Mind Horror
mobs.what: Slow, weak, jam-filled-kickball floating brains with dangling tentacles; psionic headache that high-Intelligence Crawlers shrug off.

mobs.name: Mind Horror as Game Guide (Frank Q and Maggie My)
mobs.what: A deep, rumbly-voiced Mind Horror serving as a murderous Game Guide for Crawler killers.

mobs.name: Giant Blimp neighborhood boss (Meadow Lark kill)
mobs.what: A giant blimp boss lurking in an abandoned warehouse. Yolanda shot it down from range before it could leave its lair, with Brandon and Chris along. Its wood became the float frame.
mobs.note: Still no mob page, attack or AI text; tier is neighborhood per Yolanda's page. See backlog rb-03.

mobs.name: Satan's Lil' Hedgehogs (pulled by patch)
mobs.what: Armor-piercing-quill mob seeded here and relocated to a deeper floor about 4 d 17 h before collapse. Do not field on Floor 2.

mobs.name: Shambling Acid Impaler
mobs.what: Hairy green four-legged acid-dart spitter that Mordecai warned would be everywhere; the wiki also files it under previous seasons.
mobs.note: Open conflict X-063: no seen encounter.

mobs.name: Rot Stickers (Floor 2 listing)
mobs.what: Latch-on exploding mobs from Floor 1 that the Floor 2 infobox also lists, with no Floor 2 encounter on record.
mobs.note: Open conflict X-080: treat as a Floor 1 mob unless a Floor 2 cite turns up.

hazards.name: Psionic headache
hazards.what: A health-sapping headache that can be felt before the monster is seen; weak against high Intelligence. The wiki notes a Crawler with an Intelligence of 3 feels it early.

features.name: Meadow Lark trains on Mind Horrors
features.what: The Meadow Lark fighters grind a Mind Horror quadrant between the first saferoom and the stairwell hunt.

zones.name: The Rage Elemental and the bathroom penalty
zones.name_note: Canon: a Wandering/summoned boss pulled from Floor 13 as a penalty. Not an encounter you roll on the floor.
zones.staging: A stern announcement says anyone human who relieves themselves outside a bathroom summons a smoke monster that kills them and their party. It happens in front of a convoy of frail elderly residents. The monster shreds through fog and arrows, reverses gravity, and then camps outside a saferoom pounding at the door, until it is lured into a stairwell hole with an oil slick and bombs.

announcement.style: Cascadia scolds with a prim "we are disappointed in the disrespect" and then states the penalty as a cheerful threat.
announcement.quote: This elemental will kill them and everyone in their party before they can get their pants back up.

mobs.name: Rage Elemental
mobs.what: Fifteen-foot black-and-purple smoke body with six obsidian-clawed legs and a horned skull. Arrows and missiles barely register, burning slows its self-heal, and it casts a limited-range Reverse Gravity. Its two known attacks are the claws and that spell.

hazards.name: Bathroom penalty
hazards.what: Any human who relieves themselves outside a designated bathroom summons the elemental on the spot; kills the offender and the party. Pets are exempt; ends at collapse.

hazards.name: Reverse Gravity
hazards.what: Flips gravity in a limited area; a convoy was flung to the ceiling.

hazards.name: Siege of the saferoom
hazards.what: The elemental pounds the door for hours; opening the door ejects it into the hall for 75 to 120 seconds, and the later closure rule removes the saferoom as a refuge.
hazards.note: A fan wiki says 90 to 120 seconds (M-901, X-087); both agree on the two-minute ceiling. The fan wiki credits Imani with the open-the-door idea (M-902, UNVERIFIED).

features.name: Killing it with the stairwell
features.what: The canon solve is a heavily prepared lure: oil slick, bombs and a stairwell hole where the descent rule destroys it. It gives no experience.
features.note: The no-experience note is wiki wording; no amounts here.

features.name: The MOAB bomb launcher (Bomb Chicken)
features.what: A ski-jump bomb ramp on a trailer towed by the chopper. Donut sits beside it and drops four kinds of bomb babies; a black lever drops a weighted chain bola and a red lever spills Goblin Oil. Carl leaves the last-resort Oh Shit Baby at the stairwell before the elemental hits it.
features.note: Crafting detail stays in ledger section 10 (K-137); no amounts here.

zones.name: Meadow Lark convoy to the stairwell
zones.staging: A convoy of frail residents on a ten-car wheelchair train threads a grub-choked hall toward a stairwell the Crawlers scouted. Everything goes right until one resident drops his pants. Survivors then wait in a saferoom while the Crawlers kill the elemental, and descend together.

announcement.style: Zev reports in as a producer: the elderly storyline is playing well with viewers.

hazards.name: Slow convoy in a swarm
hazards.what: A long train of frail NPCs is slow and an easy target for grubs and the elemental.

features.name: Meadow Lark party (Brandon, Chris, Imani, Yolanda)
features.what: Caretakers and elderly residents from a Wenatchee, WA nursing home. About thirty-nine patients set out on the train while Imani guards them; thirty-six residents go through in three wheeled people buckets with three staff, and Yolanda and Randall die on Floor 2.
features.note: The recap's 38 is the Floor 1 camp (M-910). A fan wiki says Seattle; Wenatchee is preferred (X-088).

features.name: Mistress Tiatha (Meadow Lark manager)
features.what: A drinking Game Guide who told Brandon every Borough and City boss on the early floors holds a stairwell.

zones.name: Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem (tunneled studio set-piece)
zones.name_note: Canon: Skull Empire game show hosted by Prince Maestro. Crawlers are teleported into a rented studio trailer.
zones.staging: A round-table panel show: two near-dead Crawlers frozen mid-fight are asked to guess who in other clips lives or dies, earning teleport points to save frozen friends. The studio audience chants and the host is a cruel, thin-skinned boar-like orc. Borant cannot refuse the show because the Skull Empire is a Syndicate member. A Crawler can flip the format by betting that the host cannot risk his own paid guests.

announcement.style: The host talks like a bully with a fan base: loud chants, insulting nicknames and tantrums when the interview slips.

mobs.name: Prince Maestro
mobs.what: Huge, muscular, bristle-haired boar-like orc host; cruel and egotistical, addresses Crawlers as meat.

mobs.name: Mexx-55 (greeter robot)
mobs.what: Black, metallic, frisbee-shaped greeter robot that hovers near the ceiling with one blinking blue light and a soothing, flat female voice. Mexx units run the cheap Senegal Production Systems trailers the Maestro rents.

mobs.name: Team Li Na (Li Jun, Zhang, Li Na and their manager)
mobs.what: Warehouse coworkers from China plus Li Jun's sister. Li Jun has deep acne scars; Zhang is bald and about Carl's age. Pulled onto the show mid-ambush, Zhang offers to save the others and Li Jun refuses to choose.

hazards.name: Time Freeze and teleport points
hazards.what: Guests are held in a Time Freeze; each correct guess earns one teleport point to send someone to the nearest saferoom.

features.name: Death Watch format and audience
features.what: Round-table guests, a studio of pre-teen boys chanting, not normally live; the format cannot be refused by Borant. Guests guess whether Crawlers in clips lived or died; Carl and Donut are sprung on the audience as surprise VIP guests.

features.name: The audience-flip gambit
features.what: Walking off and demanding the points be spent on yourself works because the show runs on a shoestring and the host cannot afford to endanger his paid guests.

zones.name: Borant staff, guides and drifters (Floor 2 roster)
zones.staging: Borant admins run the crawl from the edges: Zev enters in a water suit and talks like a nervous friend, Mukta never enters at all and books the paying show, and hidden Location Managers tend the set-piece storylines. Agatha wanders the floor and drops the illegal Valtay gear in the stairwell on the way out.

announcement.style: Admins speak in apologetic corporate shorthand; Mukta is curt and pay-per-appearance.
